articles.title: Data centers’ electricity use is soaring — especially in these states
articles.summary: Data center energy consumption is rising rapidly across the United States, with the highest growth concentrated in a few specific states. This trend is primarily driven by the expanding infrastructure needs of artificial intelligence and cloud computing services. As a result, regional power grids are facing significant pressure to manage the increased load while maintaining stability.

articles.title: 'Calvin and Hobbes' Best Bully Quote Is Still Among the Wisest in Comic Strip History

The article highlights how this particular quote remains a notable moment in the comic strip's history for its unexpected logic. It explores the lasting impact of the character's words despite his typical role as a simple antagonist.

articles.title: Keto diet slashes liver fat by 67% in just 4 months
articles.summary: A clinical study found that following a ketogenic diet for four to five months reduced liver fat by 67% and improved metabolic health more effectively than Mediterranean or low-fat diets. Approximately half of the participants on the keto diet saw their prediabetes indicators resolve, despite losing a similar amount of weight as those in the other groups.

articles.title: Is it OK to want a ‘normal life’ during the climate crisis?
articles.summary: As global environmental concerns intensify, many individuals are experiencing psychological tension between pursuing traditional life milestones and acknowledging the urgency of the climate crisis. This shift in perspective highlights a growing debate over how to balance personal aspirations with the collective responsibility of addressing systemic ecological challenges.

articles.title: 46 Years Later, the Most Influential Thriller of All Time Is Officially Free on YouTube

articles.title: For better mental health, how often you exercise may matter more than how hard
articles.summary: New research involving over 10,000 college students indicates that regular physical activity is more beneficial for mental health than the intensity or duration of a workout.
